description:
FOUND s496 (Fable, 2026-09-25) while designing #2060: cl-ppcre`s `*property-resolver*` must signal an error for an unknown property name (a NIL answer crashes cl-ppcre at MATCH time with "The function COMMON-LISP:NIL is undefined"), and the path that error would take -- PCL`s handling of `cl-ppcre:ppcre-syntax-error` -- turned out to be wrong for EVERY malformed pattern.

MEASURED (perl 5.40.3 vs main 3d9b3712, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s496/badpat.pl):
    my $r = eval { "a" =~ /(/ ; 1 }; print defined $r ? "matched\n" : "died: $@";
  perl: died: Unmatched ( in regex; marked by <-- HERE in m/( <-- HERE / at badpat.pl line 1.
  pcl : "warning:\n   Regex syntax error: Opening paren has no matching closing paren. at position 0 in string \"(\"" on stderr, then `matched` on stdout, exit 0.

THE THREE SITES (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp at 3d9b3712):
  ~30227  the match op:  (cl-ppcre:ppcre-syntax-error (e) (warn "Regex syntax error: ~A" e) nil)          -> a FALSE match result
  ~24015  split:         (cl-ppcre:ppcre-syntax-error (e) (warn "Regex syntax error in split: ~A" e) (list s)) -> the whole string as ONE field
  ~30418  s///:          (cl-ppcre:ppcre-syntax-error (e) (warn "Regex syntax error in s///: ~A" e) 0)      -> "no substitution made"
Each hands the program a value it then consumes; perl gives it none.  For a LITERAL pattern perl dies at compile time (before any statement runs); for an interpolated one at the match.  PCL compiles every pattern at its first use (`*pcl-scanner-cache*`), so the PCL die happens at the match/split/substitution -- the same PLACE for an interpolated pattern and the closest available one for a literal (USER ruling s494: fail in the same places, tidy, text free).

FIX SHAPE (rule 11): ONE helper `%pcl-regex-compile-die` (or the like) that turns a `ppcre-syntax-error` into a perl-shaped `p-die` carrying the pattern text -- perl`s words where cheap (`Unmatched ( in regex; marked by <-- HERE in m/PAT <-- HERE /`), cl-ppcre`s message otherwise -- and all three sites call it.  The die is trappable (`$@` set, program continues after an eval), and NEVER a warning.  #2060`s resolver signals a `cl-ppcre:ppcre-syntax-error` (via cl-ppcre`s `signal-syntax-error`) for an unknown / empty / unknown-user-defined property name so it takes this exact path -- one mechanism for every pattern that cannot compile.

BREAKING CASES to probe: a pattern that is INVALID in cl-ppcre but VALID in perl -- that is a translation gap, not a compile error, and today it is ALSO silently swallowed by these handlers (so this fix will surface translation gaps as dies: each one is a finding to FILE, not to hide again).  Grep the sweep`s .faillog and the companion for "Regex syntax error" BEFORE the fix to know the population.  A `qr//` object built from a bad pattern: perl dies at the qr; PCL builds the scanner at first use -- probe where the die lands.  A bad pattern inside `eval "..."` string eval.  `split` with a bad LITERAL pattern.  `$str =~ /$pat/` where `$pat` comes from user input (the case the die matters most: a program can `eval` it, which today it cannot).

BAR: gate; FULL sweep (movers = patterns that silently no-matched and now die -- each explained); companion legs for files that carried "Regex syntax error" warnings; 3 guard rows (one per op) inverse-verified on a base extraction.

SCHEDULED: member 0 of the #2060 batch (brief ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s496/s496a/prompt.md, label s496a).

=== DONE (s496a) ===
ONE helper %pcl-regex-compile-die, called from %pcl-create-scanner (every scanner is built there), turns any cl-ppcre:ppcre-syntax-error into a trappable perl-shaped die (%p-die-error): "<reason> in regex; marked by <-- HERE in m/<pattern> <-- HERE <rest>/".  The three warn+value handlers (split, match, s///) are DELETED.  qr// stays lazy: its bad pattern dies at the first USE, not at the qr (ir-spec §10-prop says so).
Guards: Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t rows 36-38 (match / split / s///, perl-compared, inverse-verified on b6560c21).
THE DIE SURFACED SIX TRANSLATION GAPS (they used to be silent no-matches); four fixed in the owning mechanism: useless inline flags (?c)(?g)(?o) dropped with the charset letters; perl 5.38's optimistic (*{...}) stripped + announced like (?{...}); a /x qr ending inside a # comment stringifies with perl's trailing newline; perl's internal \p{_Perl_IDStart} & co generated (guards regexp-subst-01.t rows 39-40).  Two stay dies (a no-match is a wrong value): recursion (?1) -> #2382, code-block CONDITION (?(?{..})..) -> #2383; possessive a++ -> #2380; control verbs (*SKIP)(*FAIL)(*:X) were already "left in, rejected" and now die.
Companion cost of the two residual dies: t/re/pat_advanced.t 1262 -> 698 C_ok (stops at line 1122, (?1)), t/re/pat.t 245 -> 206 ((?(?{..}))), t/re/pat_rt_report.t 2459 -> 2431 ((*:B) line 872).  Sweep: no mover.
subject: a regex COMPILE error is a `warn` plus a WRONG VALUE in PCL -- match answers no-match, `split` answers the whole string as one field, `s///` answers 0 -- where perl DIES at compile, trappable: `eval { "a" =~ /(/; 1 }` prints `matched` under PCL, `died: Unmatched ( in regex ...` under perl.  Rule 12 (the value flows onward).  ONE helper for the three handlers; #2060`s unknown-property die rides the same path
